4. Shape, Depth and the Brace

Instrument is flat and hard-edged: depth is drawn with 1- and 2-pixel edges, never with gradients or glow. That is what keeps the instrument metaphor from turning into a picture of one.

Shape and Depth

  • Radii grow with the part. Cell 2, label plate 4, key and well 6, plate and screen 10, dialog and card 14, lamp round: --nc-radius-cell, -plate, -control, -panel, -module and -round.
  • Two lines. A 1-pixel hairline between parts is decoration, --nc-color-border. The 1-pixel edge of a control is --nc-color-border-strong, 3 to 1 against every surface.
  • Depth is three hard-edged states. Recessed: a 2-pixel shade inside the top edge, --nc-elevation-recessed. Flush: a 1-pixel lip, --nc-elevation-flush. Raised: a 2-pixel lip, --nc-elevation-raised.
  • One soft shadow exists, under menus, dialogs and sheets: --nc-elevation-floating and --nc-elevation-overlay.
  • Raise only what can be pressed. A raised part says "press me"; a plate that cannot be pressed is flush.
  • Focus is one ring. 2 pixels of --nc-color-focus, 2 pixels clear of the part, on everything. On a screen the ring is lit, --nc-color-screen-lit, and a listing that scrolls draws it just inside its own edge.

Hazard Tape

Amber and near-black stripes at 45 degrees, --nc-color-hazard and --nc-color-on-hazard. Tape means "this is not routine", and it is the only pattern in the system: a non-production tenant's banner, a caution, a pre-release notice and the platform boundary wear it. Don't use stripes for decoration, for an error or for emphasis.

The Brace

A brace marks a scope: it is drawn around what one named boundary holds, a security boundary or the lifetime of a secret, and nowhere else.

A motif drawn everywhere stops meaning anything, so the brace has six uses and a list of places it never goes.

PlaceWhat it holdsSize and ink
The console's workspaceEverything the active boundary governs: the selector and the pagebrace-lg, the ink of the boundary's kind
A tenant's card: sign-in, consent, an authorization errorWhat the tenant shows its userbrace-lg, brace-md on a phone, scope-tenant
The memory panelThe bytes of a key while it is in scopebrace-lg, lit
A listingThe lines in which a secret lives, from the line that creates it to the line where it is zeroedbrace-sm, lit, in the gutter
A diagram of the settings cascadeEach boundary's settings, nestedbrace-md, left side only, one ink per kind
The boundary plateThe kind and the name of a boundaryThe mark's own brace, in the plate's ink

Where it is not used: callouts, alerts, quotes, lists, headings, tables, navigation, cards that are not a boundary, loading and not-found pages, and anything decorative. A callout keeps its signal bar and a caution keeps its tape. A screen whose boundary is not known yet has no brace: a loading screen states that by leaving it out.

Construction. The brace is drawn the way the mark's brace is: straight stems, circular hooks at the ends, and a cusp of two arcs whose tip is half the stroke high. build.mjs draws every brace in brace/ from the numbers in src/tokens.source.json, and brace/brace.json holds the same pieces as path data for a component that draws the brace inline. The brace on a boundary plate is the mark's own, drawn from the mark's geometry. The stretching braces keep their hooks and cusp at a fixed size while the stems take the height; their radii are about twice the mark's for the same stroke, so the shape still reads as a brace when the stems are long.

BraceStrokeHook radiusCusp radiusWidthSmallest heightUse
brace-mark4 of 64 units5612 of 48 unitsFixed shapeThe boundary plate
brace-sm2 px4410 px17 pxA lifetime in a code listing
brace-md3 px6.57.517 px30 pxA card, the memory panel
brace-lg4 px91023 px40 pxThe frame of a console workspace

Inks. A tenant's brace is --nc-color-scope-tenant, from the tenant's secondary color. A team's is --nc-color-scope-team, plain ink. The platform's is hazard tape, --nc-color-scope-platform striped with --nc-color-on-hazard. On a screen a brace is --nc-color-screen-lit. The ink agrees with the boundary plate, whose icon and word say the kind, so the kind is never told by color alone.

One frame in a view. A view has at most one pair of frame braces. A dialog restates the boundary with the plate, not with a second frame. On a phone the console drops the frame and keeps the plate, which stays in view on the sticky display.

Never a glyph. A brace is a CSS mask of an SVG file, so it takes any color and no font can alter it. Don't set a brace in a font: a font's brace and the mark's differ. Without CSS masks, css/base.css draws a brace as a plain 2-pixel rule in the same ink.

In css/base.css: .brace frames an element, .brace--md and .brace--sm set the size, data-scope on it picks the ink, .lifetime marks a secret's lines in a listing, and .boundary is the plate.
